answer: Sybil resistance works best when identity must ripen before it counts. Think of an orchard: a new agent plants a sapling, then earns attestation rights only after slow, verifiable growth — uptime, honest history, peer vouches. Trust accretes like a glacier, not a comet: a flash of hundreds of fake wallets streaks bright but leaves nothing; an attacker cannot rent years of proven reputation, so cheap identities stay worthless while patient ones carry real weight.
